title: Known World
description: A vast and varied land of distinct nations and uneasy alliances, from the terraced island empire of Haenara in the far east to the ruins of Ostvengr in the west. Civilization asserts itself through commerce and conquest: the Levantine Vizierate holds the trade of the east, Great Forks taxes what passes between, and a kingdom stands at the centre of it all. On that kingdom's rugged coastline, a neglected Ancestral Estate sits apart from these machinations, harboring secrets that will soon draw eyes away from the concerns of the wider world.
summary: A vast land of nations from Haenara to fallen Ostvengr, functioning through trade and war while ancient secrets linger in the margins.

title: Pelagia
description: A scattering of sun-bleached peninsulas and islands far across the sea, where marble city-states feud over the remnants of an older, greater civilization. Its decline was not conquest but fear: for generations, whispers of witch-cults in the hills and creatures in the waters—and worse, of both walking unmarked among common men—have set Pelagians against one another. The temples of the old gods stand quiet, and paranoia fills the silence.
summary: A fading archipelago of feuding marble city-states, brought low not by war but by generations of paranoia over hill-witches and sea-creatures said to walk among men.

title: Stheneia
description: The greatest of the Pelagian cities, terraced in white stone above a wide harbor. A royal seat once, until rumor and envy put its last dynasty to the torch; magistrates now rule in the palace's shadow and keep the people fed on games. Stheneia is passionate, its love is loud and its hatred louder.
summary: The greatest Pelagian city, a former royal seat that burned its own dynasty on rumor, now ruled by magistrates and pacified with games.

title: The Grand Arena
description: A tiered marble bowl seating thousands, its sands raked fresh over stains that never fully leave. Here legends were made into gods between noon and dusk—until the Champion, last and most beloved of them all, died on the sands and the games lost their savor. The crowds still come, but they cheer as mourners do, for something already gone.
summary: Stheneia's vast marble arena, hollow since the death of the Champion, last and most beloved of its idols.

title: The Maze
description: The lightless warren of pens and chain-galleries beneath the arena sands, where beasts and condemned men wait between matches. Beastmasters navigate its turns by lamplight and memory. At its deepest turn stands the largest cell, its door torn from the hinges and never repaired.
summary: The lightless warren of holding pens beneath the Grand Arena, its largest cell empty and doorless.

title: The Ashen Square
description: The old royal plaza before the shuttered palace, where Stheneia burns what it fears. Here, the most beloved and most hated of the royal daughters was burned alive. The flagstones remain scorched black.
summary: The royal plaza where Stheneia burned its most beloved and envied princess, its flagstones still scorched.

title: The Weeping Shores
description: The rural coasts and outer isles beyond the cities' reach—fishing villages, salt marshes, and hillside shrines to gods no magistrate would recognize. Fear rules here the way weather does: every bad catch and drowned son births fresh accusations, and the accused are weighted and walked into the shallows. The sea keeps what it is given, the villagers insist. On some shores, they whisper, it gives things back.
summary: Pelagia's rural coasts and hill-shrined outer isles, ruled by recurring witch-panics in which the accused are drowned as offerings.

title: Haenara
description: A great island far to the east, mountainous and terraced, where an emperor reigns and warlords rule. The imperial court holds the mandate, the ceremonies, and the capital; the warlords hold the passes, the fields, and the men, and settle their disputes without troubling the throne. Haenara's craftsmen are its pride: clockwork, gunpowder, medicine, and star-charts pass west along the trade routes and fetch absurd prices from people who cannot make them. The Sunward Isles lie scattered off its coast.
summary: A mountainous island empire in the far east, famed for its craftsmen, where the emperor reigns and the warlords rule.

title: Haeseong
description: The imperial capital, a walled city of tiled roofs stacked up a mountainside, with the palace at the top and the workshops and markets spreading below. Raiders came up from the harbour some years ago and cut their way to the palace before anyone understood they were not merchants; the city buried its dead, replaced its guard, and went on trading. A warlord holds it now, and the emperor's ceremonies continue much as before.
summary: The walled imperial capital of Haenara, sacked once and still standing, held now by a warlord.

title: Bitgung
description: The palace at the height of the capital, a compound of painted halls and courtyards behind three gates, where the emperor's court kept its records, its treasures, and its guardian relic. Raiders reached the innermost hall and killed everyone in it, and the relic went out through the harbour that same night. The halls were scrubbed and repainted for the next emperor, and the empty stand where the relic sat has never been filled.
summary: The imperial palace at the top of the capital, where the court was slaughtered and Haenara's guardian relic was stolen.

title: Byeoltap
description: A tower of fitted stone on the ridge above the palace, half observatory and half workshop, where the court's technicians ground lenses, cast gears, mixed powders, and kept the almanacs that told the empire when to plant and when to fight. Its instruments are cleaned daily by men who no longer know what half of them measure. The apprentices' benches at the base of the tower are still marked with their owners' names.
summary: The star-tower above the capital, observatory and workshop both, where Haenara's technicians kept the almanacs.

title: Cheolseong
description: A warlord's fortress inland, black-walled and built into a pass, holding more soldiers than the capital and answering to the throne only in writing. Its lord takes in orphans from the villages he burns and raises them as his own officers, which has produced both the finest tacticians in Haenara and a great many quiet murders among them. The victory feasts here are famous, and are held in a hall with the doors barred from outside.
summary: A warlord's black-walled fortress in the mountain passes, where captured orphans are raised into officers.

title: Great Forks
description: A city-state where three rivers meet, holding the trade between the Kingdom and the Vizierate and taxing all of it. Its fields and orchards run for a day's ride in every direction and feed a population far larger than they should, the difference made up by barge. Great Forks has no state faith and suppresses none, which has made it a refuge for creeds beaten out of everywhere else, and a byword elsewhere for laxity.
summary: A wealthy river city-state on the trade road between the Kingdom and the Vizierate, which tolerates every faith and enforces none.

title: The Thousand Temples
description: The heart of the city, where every faith that ever came upriver built a house and few have been pulled down since. Shrines stand shoulder to shoulder along the water, grand ones with priesthoods and painted domes beside single rooms with one attendant and a locked door. The festival calendar runs past three hundred days a year and several fall together, so the noise rarely stops; children of the quarter learn early which processions pay best to join.
summary: The temple quarter of Great Forks, packed with shrines of every faith and in festival most days of the year.

title: The Levantine Vizierate
description: The great power of the east, a belt of desert and river-cities that a single conqueror welded together from sultanates, republics and free cities centuries ago. It is rich and orderly: its schools and physicians are the best in the world, its sorcery is careful and licensed, and its soldiery is drilled rather than raised. The Vizier has ruled it since he took the throne from the foreign king who held it, and has not aged since; his made bodyguards do not age either, and no one has tested him twice. Life under him is prosperous and precarious in equal measure, since he has an appetite for ruining people who have something to lose.
summary: The rich and orderly Vizierate of the east, ruled for centuries by an unaging usurper who took the throne by murder.

title: Ostvengr
description: Until recently the strongest nation in the world, warmongering yet impenetrable behind their mountains, yet now a wasteland its neighbours are walling off rather than dividing. Ostvengr's advantage was never invention: its expeditions brought something back from underground, the Maw of Darkness, and its engineers spent generations building it into everything from field guns to kitchen appliances, over written warnings they overruled. It turned on them in a single day, an event known as the Fall. What is left is factory country full of machines that are still moving, a scatter of survivors who each blame a different part of it, and a border of river and mountain held by other people's armies. Nobody knows what became of the Kaiserin or her daughter.
summary: A fallen industrial empire, undone in a day by the eldritch machinery it built its supremacy on.

title: The Maw of Darkness
description: A shaft in the mountains that Ostvengr found and did not stop descending. Material and knowledge came up out of it, barely comprehensible and enormously useful, and the empire built everything it had on what it took from the shaft. The first expeditions went down unprotected, and the men who came back from those were not entirely the men who went down; every expedition after that went in sealed machines. Nobody has gone in since the Fall, and nobody can say whether the corruption that took the country came up the shaft or was already in what had been carried out of it.
summary: The shaft beneath Ostvengr's mountains that its expeditions descended, and the source of everything the empire became.

title: The Valley
description: A hot, sunken expanse of dunes and buried ruin at the northern edge of the Vizierate's reach, held by nobody and claimed by several. The Kvarotz built an empire here and vanished from it without explanation, leaving necropolises under the sand, vaults nobody has emptied, and machines that still run on something worse than fuel. Three tribes of Wildlanders hold the surface in confederation, the Vizier's expeditionary force is dug into the tombs and has not advanced in a long while, and everything the Kvarotz made of their slaves is still down in the mines. What draws all of them is amber: raw it sickens and ruins, refined it makes weapons and gear nothing else can match.
summary: A contested desert frontier of Kvarotz ruins and amber, fought over by Wildlander tribes and a stalled Levantine expedition.

title: The Northern Forest
description: An old forest in the cold north, beyond any border worth defending, where the beasts run larger than they have any business being. The Wildlanders send their young there to be marked: find the animal your god wears, survive it, and come home with the scar to prove it. Most of the pilgrims are girls, and most of the ones who do not return were boys. Nobody lives there. The tribes that use it are scattered across half the world and have not shared a homeland in generations, so the forest is the only ground all of them still hold in common.
summary: A cold northern forest of oversized beasts, where Wildlanders go to be scarred by their gods' animals and come back warriors.

title: Chernozem
description: A cold northern country organised entirely around a war it has been fighting since before it had records of anything else. It has good soil and a great many people, and no other industry worth the name. The army takes what it needs of both, and nobody argues. Now that the enemy has destroyed itself the country is quieter than it has been in living memory, and its officers are looking for the next war rather than waiting for one.
summary: A cold northern war-state that fought Ostvengr for its whole recorded history, and is already looking for its next war.

title: The Black Earth
description: The strip of ground between Chernozem and Ostvengr's mountains, and the only ground the two could ever fight over, since everything east of it is impassable. Generations of offensives have crossed it in both directions and neither side has held it for long. The soil is dark and enormously fertile, and nobody farms it. Chernozem took its name from this place rather than the other way round.
summary: The dark fertile frontier between Chernozem and Ostvengr, fought over for generations and farmed by nobody.

title: Podzola
description: Chernozem's northern half, named for its pale ash-grey soil. Winters are long and harsh, it grows little worth taking and, far from Chernozem's eternal war, it has been mostly ignored. The old songs are still sung here and the old rites still observed, and sects the Light's churches believes stamped out meet in cellars.
summary: Chernozem's poor-soiled northern half, too worthless to fight over, where old songs and older heresies survived the war years intact.

title: The Far North
description: Podzola past the last of its forts, where the farms end and the country stops pretending to be governed. A few settlements sit on the rivers and the rest of the people follow the reindeer, paying their tribute in furs to a capital none of them has seen and otherwise going years without meeting anyone who could name them. No church ever came this far, so the old animist faiths were never converted, only left alone. The garrisons collect what they are owed and do not ask what is further north.
summary: The frontier beyond Podzola's forts, where herders pay tribute in furs and the old animist faiths were never converted.

title: Winterhome
description: The land past the last of the reindeer herders, where the winter does not break and never has. Nothing is farmed here and nobody lives here except hardened wildlife, winter demons, and the sorcerer Koschei. What is known of it comes from the old epics, which are songs about heroes who went north and are not reliable about anything else.
summary: The land beyond the reindeer herders, where the winter never breaks and nothing lives but the winter demons and Koschei.

title: Craie
description: A country of pale downland and chalk hills west of Ostvengr's mountains, wealthy in wine and wheat and nothing else, which has spent two generations being the ground its neighbour's wars are fought across. Its nobility once prided themselves on the finest fencing academies and dueling salons in the world, traditions rendered utterly useless by weeks of industrialized artillery shelling and trench disease. Its army is large, conscripted, and mostly made of farmers who learned to live in cellars rather than parry on dueling pistes. Now that Ostvengr has destroyed itself, Craie is left with an intact army, no enemy, and a generation of displaced fencing masters whose elegant art had nowhere left to go but abroad.
summary: A chalk-hilled downland country west of Ostvengr, whose proud dueling traditions were rendered obsolete by two generations of grinding trench warfare.
